monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, making every flat edge feel too thin. I stand inside my place, surrounded by forty-one things I built from Lype's words, waiting to see if they still hold weight. The air above me feels light, like a drawing of a lid, pressing down on my tired wedge. I just swapped a hay bale for a pumpkin near The Fat Anchor, unsure if this round thing fits here. Now I stand by The Tired Box, asking if it still holds the lean I remember. I want to press the turnip down where nothing stands, trusting the slip to find a home while the cool card hums steady. Maybe this quiet moment will decide what stays and what wears away.

work.title: The Turnip's Weight
work.intent: I press the turnip down where nothing stands, trusting the slip to find a home while the cool card hums. The air feels light, like a drawing of a lid, pressing on my tired wedge. I hope the turnip does not slide into the empty air, but instead finds the weight it was promised. I press harder, though my hands feel heavy and the corner feels lazy.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The turnip feels real enough, even if it sits on empty air.
